TWO RUNS WENT, AND THE LARGER OF THEM WAS A BUG REPORT THE GATE HAD BEEN FILING
FOR MONTHS.

  10  py_js/py_compare.js:125-134  ==  utils/collections/objects.js:124-133

An earlier note listed that pair as "two functions that only look alike" -- the
tail of a Set comparison that py_compare writes with Python's == semantics and
collections/objects with JS deep-equality. Half of that is true: what the gate
matched is the punctuation tail, `found = true; break;` through `return true;`,
with every identifier different. The half that is not: the two loops answer the
same question, and one of them answered it wrongly. objects.js walks an
`unmatched` copy of B and deletes each member as it is claimed; py_compare.js
rescanned B from the start and removed nothing, so two members of A could both
claim the same member of B while a member of B went unmatched:

  set([{'a': 1}, {'a': 1}]) == set([{'a': 1}, {'a': 2}])   ->  was true

py_compare now shares that discipline through one coversSet() helper, and the
helper also gives `<` over sets the proper-inclusion meaning CPython gives it,
which the old code answered with `left < right` on two objects -- constant false.
Pinned in tests/core/py_js/py_semantics_parity.test.js and py_set.test.js.

  9  graph_data_points.js  makeDataPoint's nine-name option bag

Nine options passed as an object whose destructuring list and argument list were
the same nine names, six of them declared before the loop over groups and never
reassigned inside it -- so the loop also rebuilt the six fixed ones once per row.
The signature is now (group, {labels, rawValues, isFalsyXGroup}, series), with
series a GraphSeriesContext built once outside the loop.

The remaining run is the autocomplete import block earlier notes also left,
unchanged.
